decisions.reason: The theorem body already conditioned CW type on both base and fibre having CW homotopy type, but the title omitted those hypotheses and therefore asserted a false unconditional conclusion. The title was corrected, and the proof now also establishes the CGWH preservation actually needed by the projective and flag consumers.

The claimed inheritance of compact generation by arbitrary open subsets was too broad, but the required conclusion for BSO(n) is true: BO(n) is paracompact Hausdorff CGWH, and the repaired compact-fibre lemma proves that its numerable two-sheeted cover is again CGWH. The universal-class correspondence itself is unchanged.

The page's former admissible-base definition omitted CGWH, whereas the projective-bundle theorem requires a paracompact Hausdorff CGWH base of CW homotopy type. Since existence and uniqueness of the defining coefficients depend on that theorem, the broader carrier was not licensed. The definition and its F1 now state the exact hypothesis.

The proof applied the projective-bundle theorem at intermediate flag stages without an interface supplying its CGWH hypothesis. This is load bearing for injectivity. The compact-fibre lemma now proves CGWH preservation, and the splitting statement and F2 state the exact paracompact Hausdorff CGWH and CW-type scope.

F5 did overstate the projective-bundle theorem at total rank zero, where there is no projective space, tautological class, or basis ending at x^{-1}. The proof already treated zero-rank summands separately; F5 now restricts its projective-bundle assertion to m+n at least one and explicitly excludes the meaningless zero-rank relation.

The rejected interface does supply the needed classifying map after specialization to rank one. For L over B, the projective-bundle convention identifies P(L) with B and gamma_L with L, while the tautological-class definition supplies c:P(L) to RP-infinity classifying gamma_L. Thus c is exactly a classifying map for L and step 1.1 is licensed.

The supplied splitting interface explicitly states that Fl(E) is paracompact Hausdorff CGWH of CW homotopy type, and its flag-bundle construction verifies the same property at every intermediate projective stage. Therefore the naturality and line-bundle arguments on Fl(E) are within their declared admissible-base scope.

For a rank-zero bundle, normalization identifies the Thom class with the supplied orientation o in H^0(B;R), while both structural maps are identities. Hence e(0_B,o)=o, not 1 for every orientation; only the standard unit orientation gives 1. The definition, fact interface, and verification now carry this distinction.

F4 supplied the canonical pullback bundle map and pulled-back zero section, but did not itself construct disk and sphere bundles. The missing map follows after choosing the pulled-back metric: the canonical map preserves its norm exactly, so the defining disk inequality and sphere equality give a map of pairs. The proof and dependency metadata now perform this construction explicitly.

For disconnected B, H^0(B;R) contains independently chosen componentwise values, so multiplication by e(E) can have a noncyclic image. The proof needs only the particular element e(E)=1 cup e(E): exactness puts it in the kernel of p-star, and the section makes p-star injective. The invalid cyclicity assertion was removed.

The orientation interface defines an orientation as a section of the two-sheeted orientation cover, not as selected exterior-power generators. The determinant calculation remains valid in that interface: for odd n, det(-I_n) is negative, so -id carries the orientation section o to the opposite section -o and is orientation-preserving as a map (E,o) to (E,-o). The fact and proof were rewritten accordingly.

F2 omitted the hypotheses actually needed by the vanishing proposition: AC, numerability, R-orientation, positive rank, and a base in the general Thom scope. The example's standing data satisfy them, so the conclusion is sound once they are stated. The rank-zero clause was also aligned with the repaired supplier by restricting value 1 to the standard unit orientation.

The original section s is not sphere-valued away from its zero, so it cannot pull a Thom class back along the claimed pair map and the sign computation lacked a relative class. The repair rescales s into the disk bundle, makes it sphere-valued outside a closed coordinate disk, and obtains a genuine pair map. Its local boundary degree is +1 and its absolute pullback is the Euler class by straight-line homotopy to the zero section.

The cited degree interface was based, while the lifted endpoint argument produced only an unbased homotopy, so the written invocation was not licensed by F4. The already cited quaternion lemma independently proves that rho generates pi_3(SO(3)) and, in its clause 4, that the bundle clutched by rho is nontrivial. The proof now uses that exact supplied conclusion and no based/unbased conversion.

Whitney multiplicativity and naturality alone do not remove higher classes of a line bundle, so the displayed top-class calculation lacked a rank-vanishing premise and the proposed nonzero Euler witness was unsupported. The item now directly depends on the Stiefel-Whitney definition, whose rank convention gives w_i(L)=0 for i>1 and hence w(L)=1+w_1(L); multiplying the three total classes then yields the claimed degree-three product.

reviews.reason: The repaired statement separates paracompactness, compact generation, and CW-type hypotheses. Regularity of the paracompact Hausdorff base plus May's open-subspace criterion makes chart domains compactly generated; products with the compact fibre are compactly generated, and an open-chart argument gives the total space the same property. Schon's fibration theorem supplies CW type only under the explicit CW-type hypotheses.

The repaired definition makes the page-wide admissible class explicitly paracompact Hausdorff CGWH of CW homotopy type. The oriented universal model belongs to this class because its numerable two-point cover over BO(n) satisfies every clause of the strengthened compact-fibre total-space lemma, so c(gamma_n^+) is well typed.

The repaired carrier assumes exactly the paracompact Hausdorff CGWH and CW-homotopy-type conditions used by the projective-bundle theorem. Under those hypotheses the free module basis gives a unique monic degree-n relation, so all coefficients and rank conventions in the definition are well typed.

Every successive projective or finite fibre-product stage is now proved paracompact Hausdorff CGWH of CW homotopy type by the repaired compact-fibre lemma. Therefore the exact hypotheses of the projective-bundle theorem hold at each stage, each pullback is injective, and the composite splitting argument is licensed.

The positive-total-rank proof uses the projective-bundle theorem only for E direct-sum F of rank m+n at least one. When both ranks are zero, the separately stated rank convention w(0)=1 proves the formula without P(0) or a tautological x. Thus the repaired fact interface covers every branch without an ill-defined x^{-1} basis.

In rank one, P(L) is B and its tautological line is L. The cited definition then constructs a map from P(L)=B to RP-infinity whose pullback of the universal line is gamma_L=L. Naturality fixes the value on every line bundle, and injective pullback to the repaired flag space proves equality for arbitrary finite rank, so no content edit is required.

The real splitting theorem now expressly guarantees that Fl(E) is a paracompact Hausdorff CGWH base of CW homotopy type and that q-star is injective. Hence all uses of Stiefel-Whitney naturality and the rank-one orientability calculation on Fl(E) are well typed, and injectivity returns the equivalence to B without any repair to this item.

The repaired rank-zero branch follows directly from fiber normalization: u restricts to the chosen orientation o at every point and therefore equals o in degree zero. Since the disk bundle is B, the sphere bundle is empty, and j and s are identities, the Euler class is o; the unit formula is explicitly limited to o=1.

With h-prime defined by the pullback norm, the canonical map Phi(b-prime,v)=v sends norm at most one to norm at most one and norm one to norm one, yielding the required pair map. The zero-section square commutes by the pullback-section formula, pair-sequence naturality commutes with relative-to-absolute maps, and Thom naturality identifies Phi-star u_E with u_{f-star E}; the Euler naturality equation now follows with no unstated interface.

A normalized nowhere-zero section is a right inverse to the sphere projection, so p-star has a left inverse and is injective. In the degree-n Gysin segment, exactness identifies the image of multiplication by e(E) with ker p-star. Since the unit maps specifically to e(E), injectivity forces e(E)=0 without any connectedness or cyclic-image claim.

In oriented local frames, -id has matrix -I_n and determinant sign (-1)^n. For odd n this exchanges the two sheets of the orientation cover, hence gives an orientation-preserving isomorphism (E,o) to (E,-o) over the identity. Naturality equates their Euler classes while the orientation-sign law negates them, yielding e=-e and therefore 2e=0.

For positive n, the product bundle is numerable and R-oriented over the stipulated Thom-scope base, and its explicit constant section (b,e_1) is continuous and nowhere zero; the repaired proposition therefore gives zero. In rank zero, normalization returns the supplied orientation o, so the example correctly asserts value 1 only for the standard unit orientation.

On a closed w-disk D, the repaired section has fiber coordinate w divided by the positive factor epsilon a(w), and outside its interior it is the unit normalization of s. The boundary formulas agree and yield a map (M,M-minus-int D) to (D(L),S(L)). Its pullback Thom class has absolute image e(L), while excision identifies its local map with a positive degree-one radial rescaling, so the Euler number is +1 and c1(gamma) restricts to -x as claimed.

The witness is the bundle E_rho named in clause 4 of the quaternion lemma, which directly states that the clutching bundle is nontrivial; clauses 2 and 3 also identify [rho] as a generator of pi_3(SO(3)). Its Euler class vanishes because H^3(S^4;Z)=0. A nowhere-zero section would split off a line, and the complementary oriented two-plane is trivial because every S^3-to-S^1 clutching map lifts to contractible R, contradicting E_rho's nontriviality.

For each line L the defining rank convention gives w(L)=1+w_1(L). Whitney multiplication therefore gives w(E)=(1+a)(1+b)(1+a+b), so w_1(E)=a+b+a+b=0 and w_3(E)=ab(a+b), a nonzero sum of distinct monomials in F_2[a,b]. Orientability follows from w_1=0; mod-two reduction sends the integral Euler class to this nonzero w_3, while odd rank gives 2e=0, proving that e is nonzero of order two.
